result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS: ISS-0783 cannot be reproduced as described because its subject does not exist. This is not a 'reproduced and root-caused' PASS -- it is a finding that the issue's premise is false, which is itself the correct diagnostic output for CODE-DESIGNER/ORCH to act on (there is nothing to design a fix for).

WHAT I CHECKED, DIRECTLY, NOT FROM THE ISSUE'S PROSE:

1. File existence. `web/src/auth/TenantSwitcher.tsx` does not exist. Directory listing of web/src/auth/ (read directly): AuthContext.tsx, AuthProvider.tsx, OidcManager.ts, ProtectedRoute.tsx, __tests__/, buildRedirectArgs.test.ts, oidcRedirectArgs.ts, safeRestorePath.ts, tenantConfig.test.ts, tenantConfig.ts, tokenUtils.ts, useTenantContext.ts -- no TenantSwitcher.tsx, no TenantSwitcher anywhere in web/src (grep -ril "TenantSwitcher" web/ returns only docs/issues/ISS-0783.yaml itself). `find web/src -iname "*tenant*"` lists tenantConfig.ts/.test.ts, useTenantContext.ts, api/tenants.ts, components/layout/TenantHeader.tsx, and admin tenant-management pages -- none is a switcher component and none contains an onSelect handler over a set of tenant options.

2. Symbol existence. `grep -ril "switchingToTenantSlug" .` across the whole repo returns only docs/issues/ISS-0783.yaml and this run's own step-00.5 handoff -- the symbol does not exist in any source file. AuthProvider.tsx was read in full (149 lines): its exported context value is `{ session, isAuthenticated, isLoading, loginSource, login, logout, setSession }`. There is no `switchTenant` function, no `switchingToTenantSlug` state, no `outgoingTenantId` closure variable, and no `removeQueries` call anywhere in the file. The only session-mutating functions are `login` (OIDC token decode + tenant lookup, sets full session), `logout` (clears token, resets tenant-config cache, redirects to Keycloak signout), and `setSession` (a plain passthrough setter). None of these implement a same-tab tenant switch; `logout`'s own comment confirms company changes go through a full OIDC sign-in/sign-out redirect (`resetTenantConfigCache` + `signoutRedirect`), i.e. a full page navigation, not an in-app switch.

3. History. `git log --all -S "switchTenant" --oneline` (a pickaxe search across every commit and every branch tip reachable from --all, not just this branch) returns exactly two hits: 2dddbf71 (the commit that filed ISS-0783.yaml itself) and 08f41e1f (this run's own step-00.5 dispatch handoff) -- i.e. the string 'switchTenant' has never appeared in any tracked source file, only in this issue's own paperwork. `git log --oneline --all -- "*TenantSwitcher*"` returns nothing -- no file by that name has ever existed at any point in this repo's history, including on other branches. `git show 23a67263` (the commit ISS-0783 cites as the fix pass that narrowed switchingToTenantSlug's lifetime) fails: 'fatal: ambiguous argument 23a67263: unknown revision or path not in the working tree' -- that commit does not exist in this repository.

4. The requirement ISS-0783 claims to have been discovered during. ISS-0783.yaml states `discovered_in_run: WF02-REQ384-20260922` and describes discovery 'during REQ-384's OIDC silent-callback fix pass'. docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-384 entry ('In-app company/tenant switcher for a dual-membership user...') has `status: pending`, `depends_on: []`, and its own description -- written when the requirement was filed, 2026-09-20 -- states as its own justification: 'There is no in-app company/tenant selector anywhere in web/src -- grepped exhaustively (...no switchCompany/switchTenant/CompanySelector symbol exists anywhere in web/src).' That statement is still independently true today per my own grep above. docs/status/requirement_status.v20.yaml has no 'started' (or any) event for REQ-384 anywhere -- the only mention is a note that a sibling session's concurrent work ('ISS-0737, REQ-384/385, unrelated tenant-switch-cache-isolation scenario') was picked up cleanly by a `git pull --ff-only`, i.e. REQ-384 was filed but has never had a WF-02 implementation pass run against it, on this branch or any other reachable from --all.

CONCLUSION -- ROOT CAUSE OF THE ISSUE REPORT ITSELF (not of a code defect): ISS-0783 describes a re-entrancy bug in a UI component and a state-lifetime interaction (TenantSwitcher.tsx's onSelect handler vs. AuthProvider's switchingToTenantSlug) that were never implemented. REQ-384, the requirement that would create this component, is still `status: pending` with zero implementation history. The issue's own narrative -- 'once switchingToTenantSlug was correctly narrowed... TenantSwitcher.tsx's trigger/option buttons are no longer implicitly disabled' -- presupposes a fix pass (commit 23a67263) and a SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER sign-off during 'REQ-384's WF-02 pipeline' that never happened; the cited commit does not exist and no such pipeline run appears anywhere in docs/status/. This is a fabricated/hallucinated issue report, analogous to the self-assigned/fabricated queue-id pattern already on record in docs/anti-patterns.md (REQ-382/383/384/385's impl_order comments all note corrected fabricated ids), except here the fabrication is the discovery narrative and root-cause trace of the issue itself, not just a queue id. Note that ISS-0782 (this run's sibling issue, same discovered_in_run label 'WF02-REQ384-20260922', filed by the same batch) is NOT similarly fabricated -- its identity.ts routing defect was independently reproduced against a real running backend (see handoffs/WF03-ISS0782-20260923/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json) and is real, so 'WF02-REQ384-20260922' as a discovered_in_run label is not itself proof of fabrication across the board -- ISS-0783 specifically fails on its own, separately-checked facts (file/symbol/commit non-existence), independent of that shared label.

REPRODUCTION EVIDENCE (real, not restated): wrote a throwaway Vitest test at web/src/auth/__tests__/ISS-0783-throwaway-repro.test.tsx asserting `import('../TenantSwitcher')` rejects, and ran it with `npx vitest run src/auth/__tests__/ISS-0783-throwaway-repro.test.tsx` from web/. Actual output:

  RUN  v2.1.9 C:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow/web
  ✓ src/auth/__tests__/ISS-0783-throwaway-repro.test.tsx (1 test) 7ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  1 passed (1)

The import rejects (module resolution failure), confirming directly -- not from the bug report's prose -- that TenantSwitcher.tsx is not resolvable as a module in this codebase today. The throwaway test file was deleted immediately after this run (`rm web/src/auth/__tests__/ISS-0783-throwaway-repro.test.tsx`); `git status --short web/` after deletion shows no residue from it (only a pre-existing untracked web/tests/e2e/.pipeline-state/ directory unrelated to this task).

WHY 'acceptance criterion 3' (root cause traced to exact TenantSwitcher.tsx lines/handlers) CANNOT BE SATISFIED AS WORDED: there are no lines or handlers to cite -- the file does not exist. Likewise AuthProvider.tsx's switchingToTenantSlug lifetime cannot be re-confirmed because the field itself does not exist in AuthProvider.tsx (see full-file read above); the closest re-confirmable fact is the negative one -- AuthProvider.tsx has no tenant-switch-related state of any kind.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PIPELINE (not a fix-design handoff): CODE-DESIGNER should not be asked to design a fix for a component that doesn't exist. Two legitimate paths forward, ORCH's call: (a) if an in-app tenant switcher is wanted, that is REQ-384's own still-pending scope (build the switcher AND its cache-isolation guarantee, per REQ-384's acceptance criteria, which already anticipate needing an in-flight/pending-guard concern once a switcher exists) -- ISS-0783 should be closed as invalid/superseded-by-REQ-384 rather than worked as a standalone fix, since 'fixing' a re-entrancy guard on a component that isn't built yet is not meaningful; or (b) if ORCH intends this run to continue exercising the standalone-issue-fix pipeline shape regardless, the only defensible fix target left is to build the guard as part of REQ-384 itself when that requirement is eventually implemented, and ISS-0783 should be re-filed (or amended) as a note/acceptance-criterion addendum on REQ-384 rather than a freestanding WF-03 issue. Recommend ORCH re-triage docs/issues/ISS-0783.yaml's `status` (currently `open`) to `invalid` or `superseded`, with a note pointing at this diagnosis, rather than routing this handoff on to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design against nonexistent code. Not marking docs/issues/ISS-0783.yaml itself with a status change here, since that is DOC-UPDATER's/ORCH's step, not ISSUE-FIXER's, under WF-03 -- flagging it in this handoff's result instead.
issues: ISS-0783's subject (web/src/auth/TenantSwitcher.tsx and AuthProvider.tsx's switchingToTenantSlug) does not exist in the codebase or in any commit reachable from --all.

REQ-384, the requirement ISS-0783 claims to have been discovered during, is docs/requirements.yaml status: pending with no implementation history anywhere in docs/status/ -- it has never been built.
No fix can be designed against code that does not exist; routing this to CODE-DESIGNER as a normal WF-03 fix-design step would produce a design for a fictional component.
